{"task": {"id": "I_kwDOVRkquM8AAAABZay0qA", "item_id": "PVTI_lAHOAHSLSM4Bn_T5zhDCIBc", "project_id": "PVT_kwHOAHSLSM4Bn_T5", "number": 41, "title": "Resolve and implement VRAM read-buffer access restrictions", "body": "## Problem

VRAM address writes and read-buffer refills currently fetch software-addressed VRAM regardless of display state. This is the next unresolved behavior identified in the supplied assessment, and remains explicitly unverified after Issue #39.

At baseline `c72edab2e9e49e22110a86b713d6bcf80c241f26`:

- [`Ppu::write`](https://github.com/takahirox/snes-rust/blob/c72edab2e9e49e22110a86b713d6bcf80c241f26/crates/snes-core/src/ppu.rs#L146) unconditionally prefetches on either `$2116/$2117` write.
- [`Ppu::read`](https://github.com/takahirox/snes-rust/blob/c72edab2e9e49e22110a86b713d6bcf80c241f26/crates/snes-core/src/ppu.rs#L219) returns a buffered byte and unconditionally fetches another word when the VMAIN-selected port triggers advancement.
- The [existing VRAM test](https://github.com/takahirox/snes-rust/blob/c72edab2e9e49e22110a86b713d6bcf80c241f26/crates/snes-core/src/ppu.rs#L755) checks blank-period reads and blocked active-display/HBlank writes, but never asserts restricted-period reads or prefetch results.

Consequently, the write-gating test does not establish read-access correctness. This shared PPU path also serves B-bus DMA/HDMA reads.

## Expected outcome

Implement the specification-supported restrictions on VRAM read-buffer fetches, including address-write prefetch and data-port refill, while preserving documented address progression and accessible-period reads.

Resolve the exact restricted-access contract before encoding expectations. The repository's available evidence does **not** establish whether an unavailable fetch produces zero, retains the buffer, or obtains another value. Do not invent a constant, copy the write predicate without read-specific evidence, or treat existing assertions as hardware authority.

Use these hardware references, already identified by the repository:

- [Anomie's Register Doc](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/gilligan/snesdev/master/docs/snes_registers.txt), revision 1157: entries `$2100`, `$2115`, `$2116/$2117`, and `$2139/$213A`.
- [Fullsnes](https://problemkaputt.de/fullsnes.htm): VRAM access registers, read buffering, access restrictions, and relevant display timing.

Record exact supporting sections, reference versions and content hashes. Reconcile disagreements explicitly. The prior [reference record](https://github.com/takahirox/snes-rust/blob/c72edab2e9e49e22110a86b713d6bcf80c241f26/docs/issue-39-validation.md#register-evidence-and-qualifications) identifies versions, but its cited passages concern counter latching rather than this VRAM contract.

The resulting contract must specify each operation as `(returned byte, next read buffer, next VMADD)`:

| Operation | Required distinction |
| --- | --- |
| Write `$2116` or `$2117` | Address replacement versus triggered prefetch; availability of that fetch |
| Read the non-incrementing data port | Returned buffered byte versus any buffer/address side effects |
| Read the VMAIN-selected incrementing port | Returned old-buffer byte, refill address/order, and subsequent address increment |
| Fetch during restricted display periods | Buffer result and address progression, separately from CPU/PPU open-bus effects |

Cover forced blank, ordinary VBlank, active display, HBlank, and scanline 0 explicitly. For accessible periods, recheck the existing contract: address writes prefetch the new remapped word; reads return the old buffer; a selected-port read reloads from the pre-increment address and then increments. Correct the earlier dummy-read expectations if the references contradict them.

If a reference leaves electrical bits unspecified, document that uncertainty and distinguish any deterministic emulator approximation from verified hardware semantics. This does not justify retaining a contradicted logical access rule.

### Scope and remaining work

Keep production changes focused on VRAM prefetch/read-buffer behavior and its shared CPU/B-bus routing. Retain the existing scheduler's access phases unless a narrowly necessary correction is demonstrated. CPU reads currently sample after their timed access; reverse DMA samples at transfer `+4` and commits its destination at `+8` ([source](https://github.com/takahirox/snes-rust/blob/c72edab2e9e49e22110a86b713d6bcf80c241f26/crates/snes-core/src/machine.rs#L454)). These are emulator timing conventions, not proof of physical strobe accuracy.

OAM/CGRAM restrictions, electrical bus modeling, dot-level VRAM arbitration, raster rendering, long dots, interlace/overscan, PAL, and DMA startup/alignment remain outside this Issue. `ppu-ports` remains partial. Preserve all 24 inventory categories and their outstanding scope; this change does not verify unrelated behavior.

## Context and reproduction

The [Issue #5 record](https://github.com/takahirox/snes-rust/blob/c72edab2e9e49e22110a86b713d6bcf80c241f26/docs/issue-5-validation.md#timing-and-ppu-changes-and-independent-expectations) attributes the existing buffering/write tests to hardware documentation. The [Issue #39 limits](https://github.com/takahirox/snes-rust/blob/c72edab2e9e49e22110a86b713d6bcf80c241f26/docs/issue-39-validation.md#remaining-limits) explicitly leave active-display VRAM reads unresolved. No open Issue duplicates this work in the supplied context.

Construct distinct VRAM words and an independently seeded buffer under forced blank. Release blanking, perform address writes and selected/non-selected data-port reads during active display and HBlank, then return to an accessible period and observe both buffer recovery and address progression. Baseline source predicts ordinary addressed-memory fetches throughout; compare against the resolved specification contract.

Planning inspected repository files only. The ignored reference copies mentioned by earlier records are absent from this checkout; external references were not fetched and no suites were rerun.

## Pre-merge acceptance

- [ ] Record the complete operation/state matrix above with precise source attribution before implementing restricted-fetch behavior. Explicitly resolve HBlank, scanline 0, returned-byte versus refill behavior, and increment ordering. Amend unsupported earlier contracts rather than preserving them merely to keep tests green.
- [ ] Implement the supported correction in the shared PPU register path. Demonstrate at least one source-backed counterexample that fails against the baseline and passes with the correction. A documentation-only restatement is insufficient.
- [ ] Add original Rust vectors using distinct word/byte sentinels. Cover both address-write ports, both read ports, both increment-port selections, VMAIN increments `1/32/128/128`, all four remapping selections, address wrapping, repeated reads, and accessible/restricted transitions. Derive expected values independently of production helpers.
- [ ] Add natural-scheduler tests using ordinary timed bus operations rather than injected raster or buffer state. Cover stable active display/HBlank, forced-blank changes, and accesses ending before, at, and after the model's `224→225` and `261→0` boundaries. Label model timing expectations separately from documented hardware facts.
- [ ] Exercise reverse DMA through `$2139/$213A`, including a boundary where source sampling and destination commitment occur in different display states. Add direct/indirect reverse-HDMA HBlank controls. Assert buffer/address effects and DMA destination/count/table progression; preserve existing forward VRAM-write boundary tests.
- [ ] Add an original MIT CPU-executed guest, for example `crates/snes-core/tests/ppu_vram_access.rs`. Initialize VRAM and registers through guest instructions, synchronize through hardware-visible status/IRQ, and publish numeric results in WRAM. Require a completion marker within explicit instruction/frame bounds. The host supplies only the ROM and observes results; it must not patch CPU, raster, PPU, buffer, or guest results. Document source/data/build provenance in `tests/roms/PROVENANCE.md`; acquire no commercial ROM or firmware.
- [ ] Run and pass the following existing gates plus the new focused tests:

```sh
cargo fmt --all -- --check
cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets --locked -- -D warnings
cargo test --workspace --locked
cargo test --locked -p snes-core --test ppu_vram_access
python3 tools/make-fixture.py .cache/smoke.bin
cmp tests/roms/smoke.bin .cache/smoke.bin
python3 tools/build-test-tools.py --spc
python3 tools/hardware-tests.py \
  --ca65 "$PWD/.cache/tools/cc65/bin/ca65" \
  --ld65 "$PWD/.cache/tools/cc65/bin/ld65" \
  --spcasm "$PWD/.cache/tools/spcasm/target/release/spcasm"
python3 tools/ppu-test.py \
  --bass "$PWD/.cache/tools/bass-untech/bass/out/bass-untech"
python3 tools/build-cleared-games.py
python3 tools/build-cleared-games.py
npm --prefix web ci
npm --prefix web run build
(cd web && npx playwright install chromium)
npm --prefix web test -- --grep-invert '301 seconds'
git diff --check
```

Use the compiler-selection and available-port instructions in [README](https://github.com/takahirox/snes-rust/blob/c72edab2e9e49e22110a86b713d6bcf80c241f26/README.md#validate) where needed.

- [ ] Preserve pinned fixture/game sources, licenses, ROM hashes, replay inputs, gameplay/audio assertions, Castle's full route, and both cleared five-minute game regressions. Do not weaken checks to accommodate the correction.
- [ ] Update README limitations and a focused validation record with the final contract, baseline failure, actual commands/results and remaining uncertainty. Limited test passes must not be described as full hardware accuracy, category completion, Issue #3 completion, or commercial compatibility.

## Optional validation

None required beyond the pre-merge gates. Do not acquire additional ROMs or firmware.

## Required post-merge verification

None.
